item.content:encoded:
Israel’s opposition elects Kahana speaker, gains say over legislative agenda

Category: World

Israel’s parliament elected opposition lawmaker Matan Kahana as speaker on Tuesday, giving the bloc seeking to replace caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu greater influence over the legislative agenda. Kahana, an ally of Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, won 66 votes in the 120-seat Knesset, while Likud’s candidate, Ofir Katz, received 52. Arab-led parties backed Kahana alongside Jewish opposition parties, helping secure his election after a debate lasting about seven hours [2][13][10][4]. The speaker helps set the timetable for debates and votes. Eisenkot’s bloc says it wants to reverse laws that weakened judicial powers, establish an inquiry into the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack, and introduce term limits for prime ministers. The opposition has also gained leadership of key committees, while Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister [10][3][9]. President Isaac Herzog has tasked Eisenkot with forming a coalition, but his bloc lacks a majority without Arab-party support, which some Jewish opposition leaders reject. Eisenkot has until Dec. 6 to form a government, with a possible two-week extension. His bloc has agreed not to advance repeal of the judicial overhaul before Monday, according to Ynet [21][13].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

The Knesset is the home of all citizens of the State of Israel, regardless of religion, race, or gender.

— Matan Kahana, newly elected Knesset speaker (The Times of Israel)

Did you know: The Knesset speaker can serve as Israel’s acting head of state if the president is unable to perform official duties [5].

Key Points

  • Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee chair Avigdor Lieberman said he would summon security chiefs, all appointed by Netanyahu, for oversight hearings, including on Iran [3].
  • Legislative hurdles: Bills must pass through committee and multiple floor votes, limiting how quickly legislation can pass even with the speaker’s control over scheduling [4][2].
  • Election inquiry: Israel’s Central Elections Committee said an investigation found no evidence of voter bribes on a scale that could have affected the election outcome [5][7][25].
  • Arab-party role: The two Arab-majority slates hold 19 seats; one of their lawmakers was absent from the speaker vote [13].
  • The pledge to pause repeal was part of a reported agreement in which Netanyahu’s bloc agreed not to extend its filibuster against the speaker vote [13].

Perspectives

Likud Party: The party condemned Kahana’s election as achieved with “the votes of terror supporters,” objecting to the Arab parties’ backing [13].

Sources: The Times of Israel

Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party: Eisenkot said Netanyahu was unfit to remain prime minister after allegations that people around the prime minister sought to fabricate election-fraud claims against Arab lawmakers [3].

Sources: Financial Times

Yousef Jabareen, Joint List leader: Jabareen signaled willingness to work with other parties to remove Netanyahu, saying his government had pursued a hard-line policy toward Arab citizens and Palestinians [20].

Sources: tagesschau.de

Assaf Shapira, Israel Democracy Institute researcher: Shapira warned that if Eisenkot fails to form a government, Likud could gain control of a temporary committee and slow the opposition’s legislative plans [9].

Sources: The Globe and Mail

Timeline

  • 27 October 2026: Parliamentary election left neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot with a majority [10].
  • 10 November 2026: Newly elected Knesset convened without a government in place [10].
  • 17 November 2026: Knesset elected Matan Kahana speaker by a 66-52 vote [13].
  • 6 December 2026: Eisenkot’s initial deadline to form a government; president may extend it [21].

Historical Background

Netanyahu’s government began advancing judicial changes shortly after he returned to office in December 2022; the proposals triggered large demonstrations, with tens of thousands taking to the streets [5][19].

Q&A

Q: What happens if Eisenkot cannot form a coalition?

A: President Isaac Herzog could give Netanyahu a chance to form a government; if neither succeeds, another election is expected in 2027 [2][12].

item.content:encoded:
China tariff deal offers Canadian pork exporters relief after losses

Category: Canada

China will suspend its additional 25% tariff on most frozen Canadian pork cuts from Jan. 1, 2027, under an expanded trade arrangement Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed to in Shenzhen. The deal also extends tariff relief on other Canadian exports, including seafood, while Canada extends exemptions for some Chinese steel and aluminum products [41][8][2]. The pork measures cover about C$116 million in exports and run through Dec. 31, 2028, but do not apply to every pork product. Canadian exporters have lost customers and market share since the tariffs took effect; the Canadian Meat Council says Canadian pork exports to China fell from about C$469 million in 2024 to C$354 million in 2025 [41][8]. Agriculture Minister Heath MacDonald praised the new market access, while Conservative and Bloc Québécois members criticized the partnership with China over dependence, human rights and security concerns. China’s commerce ministry said the two governments would complete domestic procedures and work to put the measures into effect [12][45].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Today's tariff relief on frozen pork cuts is welcome news for Canadian pork producers and demonstrates what sustained engagement and strong industry–government collaboration can achieve

— René Roy, chair of the Canadian Pork Council (RealAgriculture)

Key Points

  • Export losses: The Canadian Meat Council estimates exporters have lost C$126 million to date [41].
  • Pork exclusions: China’s relief covers most frozen cuts, but offal and other Canadian pork products remain outside the arrangement [8][41].
  • Seafood access: The expanded list includes Pacific spot prawns, geoduck, sea cucumber and Greenland halibut; about 16% of Canada’s fish and seafood exports went to China in 2024 [8].
  • Canola tariffs: China’s canola-seed tariff remains 14.9%, while canola oil is still subject to a 100% tariff [8].
  • Business links: Canada plans a trade mission to China in 2027 and has designated it a bilateral e-commerce year to help small and midsize firms reach Chinese consumers [43].

Perspectives

Conservative Party of Canada and Bloc Québécois: Conservative MPs argued the government was trading U.S. dependence for dependence on China; Bloc Québécois Leader Yves-François Blanchet said the agreement offered too little on human rights and raised concerns about Chinese aluminum entering Canada [12].

Sources: Le Devoir

Timeline

  • 2018: Canada detained Huawei executive Meng Wanzhou; China later detained two Canadians [19]
  • March 2025: China imposed additional tariffs affecting Canadian pork exports [41]
  • 4 November 2026: Ottawa announced two-year extensions for relief on canola meal, peas, lobster and crab [8]
  • 17 November 2026: Carney and Xi agreed to expand and extend the bilateral trade arrangement [41]
  • 1 January 2027: China's suspension of additional pork tariffs is scheduled to begin [41]

Industry Impact

  • Pork processing: Chinese consumers value a range of pork cuts, including offal, which remains outside the tariff relief [8].
  • Steel and aluminum supply: Canada expanded tariff-remission coverage to 32 Chinese steel and aluminum items—23 steel and nine aluminum—for which domestic supply is insufficient or unavailable [41].
  • Crop producers: The agreement also opens China’s market to Canadian fava beans, chickpeas and lentils [8].

Historical Background

Canada imposed a 100% tariff on Chinese electric vehicles in 2024 [19].

item.title: Alberta urges 72-hour emergency kits as national alert test nears
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (Canada / Emergency Alerts)
item.description: Alberta is urging residents to prepare emergency supplies ahead of a nationwide test of Canada’s Alert Ready system on Wednesday, Nov. 18. The test will reach television, radio and compatible wireless devices in every province and territory [1][2]. Alberta Public Safety and Emergency Services Minister Mike Ellis encouraged residents to download the provincial alert app and keep a kit with enough supplies to last at least 72 hours, including water, non-perishable food, flashlights, batteries and first-aid items [1]. The test message will identify itself as a test and say no action is required [2].
item.content:encoded:
Alberta urges 72-hour emergency kits as national alert test nears

Category: Canada

Alberta is urging residents to prepare emergency supplies ahead of a nationwide test of Canada’s Alert Ready system on Wednesday, Nov. 18. The test will reach television, radio and compatible wireless devices in every province and territory [1][2]. Alberta Public Safety and Emergency Services Minister Mike Ellis encouraged residents to download the provincial alert app and keep a kit with enough supplies to last at least 72 hours, including water, non-perishable food, flashlights, batteries and first-aid items [1]. The test message will identify itself as a test and say no action is required [2].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

These alerts can be surprising, even jarring, but that’s the point.

— Mike Ellis, Alberta Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Services (Edmonton Journal)

Key Points

  • Alert volume: Alert Ready had issued more than 1,215 emergency messages across Canada in 2026, according to the system’s operator [2].
  • Phone compatibility: Wireless devices need to support public alerts, run current software and connect to an LTE network when the alert is sent or while it remains active [3].
  • Testing rules: The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission requires broadcasters and wireless providers to issue at least one public test alert each year; tests typically occur in May and November [2].

Perspectives

Pelmorex, Alert Ready’s technical infrastructure operator, said Canadians cannot opt out of wireless alerts because the system is intended to warn them of imminent threats to life and property [2].

Sources: CBC News

item.title: Toronto police charge two, seek third after East York break-in
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (Canada / Crime)
item.description: Toronto police arrested two men and are searching for a third suspect after an attempted break-in at an East York home on Saturday evening. Police allege three people tried to enter the residence while the homeowner was inside. When the homeowner chased them, they fled in a vehicle that crashed into a nearby store. The homeowner was not injured [3][2]. Police identified the accused as Liban Mohammed, 19, and Dontae Kerr, 20, both of Hamilton. They face charges related to the attempted break-in and other alleged conduct; the allegations have not been proven in court. Investigators are asking anyone with information to contact Toronto police [3][2].
item.content:encoded:
Toronto police charge two, seek third after East York break-in

Category: Canada

Toronto police arrested two men and are searching for a third suspect after an attempted break-in at an East York home on Saturday evening. Police allege three people tried to enter the residence while the homeowner was inside. When the homeowner chased them, they fled in a vehicle that crashed into a nearby store. The homeowner was not injured [3][2]. Police identified the accused as Liban Mohammed, 19, and Dontae Kerr, 20, both of Hamilton. They face charges related to the attempted break-in and other alleged conduct; the allegations have not been proven in court. Investigators are asking anyone with information to contact Toronto police [3][2].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Key Points

  • Charges filed: Mohammed was also charged with dangerous operation of a conveyance, while Kerr faces a charge of disguise with intent [3][2].
  • Suspect description: Police describe the outstanding suspect as 18 to 22 years old with a slim build. He was last seen wearing all black [3][2].
  • Police previously described the incident as targeted [2].

item.content:encoded:
Commons sends assisted-dying bill to committee before March deadline

Category: Canada

Canada’s House of Commons voted 225-89 on Nov. 17 to send Liberal Bill C-41, which would allow advance requests for medical assistance in dying (MAID) and exclude people whose sole underlying condition is a mental illness, to committee [2][3]. The bill must pass both the Commons and Senate before March 17, when the current exclusion for people whose sole underlying condition is a mental illness expires [3][4]. The vote followed the government’s decision to limit second-reading debate, prompting Conservative and Bloc Québécois MPs to call for more scrutiny; Justice Minister Sean Fraser said debate would continue in committee [3][2]. The committee will examine the bill, while provinces would decide whether to implement advance requests through their health systems [3].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

more concerned about extending access without the safeguards in place, including the safeguards that must be legislated by provincial governments.

— Sean Fraser, Justice Minister (CBC News)

Key Points

  • Provincial choices: Quebec is the only province with an advance-request regime; Alberta has passed legislation barring advance requests for MAID [3].
  • Consent safeguards: The bill requires agreement from two independent medical or nurse practitioners and prohibits administering MAID if a person expresses refusal or resistance through words, sounds or gestures [3].
  • Advance requests: The bill would allow someone with a degenerative condition such as dementia or ALS to request MAID in advance, to be carried out after they lose the capacity to consent [3].

Perspectives

Conservative Party of Canada: The party supports excluding people whose sole condition is mental illness but urged the government to split the bill so MPs could scrutinize advance requests separately; Conservative MP Tamara Jansen said MPs still lacked the government’s analysis of possible Charter impacts [3][2].

Sources: CBC News

Sean Fraser, Justice Minister: Fraser said he wanted the Commons to pass the bill before the parliamentary sitting ends in December, leaving the Senate time to debate and pass it before the March deadline [3].

Sources: CBC News

Timeline

  • June 2026: Special committee recommended indefinite exclusion for mental-illness-only cases [3]
  • 27 October 2026: Government introduced Bill C-41 in the House of Commons [3]
  • 16 November 2026: Third day of second-reading debate, following sessions on Oct. 30 and Nov. 4 [3]
  • 17 November 2026: Commons voted 225-89 to refer Bill C-41 to committee [2]
  • 17 March 2027: Current exclusion for mental-illness-only cases is due to expire [3]

Historical Background

Parliament has repeatedly postponed the date when mental illness could qualify for MAID and referred the question to a special committee [3]. Under existing law, MAID is available to adults with a serious and incurable physical illness, disease or disability who are in an advanced or irreversible decline and can make a voluntary request and give informed consent, including at the time MAID is administered [3].

item.content:encoded:
Manitoba promises ER reopenings and middle-class tax cut before election

Category: Canada

Manitoba’s NDP government pledged to reopen Winnipeg’s Victoria Hospital emergency department by next summer and deliver a middle-class tax cut in a throne speech Tuesday that Premier Wab Kinew described as his last before the 2027 election [1][3][4]. The previous government closed Victoria’s emergency room, and reopening it was a 2023 campaign promise [3]. The province also plans to offer free shingles vaccinations to some seniors starting in July 2027 [3]. The speech also promised a new emergency room in Eriksdale by next fall and said details of the tax cut would come in next spring’s budget [1][3]. Kinew said balancing the budget remains a priority as the government pursues affordability measures [1].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

The economic horse pulls the social cart.

— Premier Wab Kinew (The Globe and Mail)

Key Points

  • Vaccine eligibility: The free two-dose Shingrix program is planned for people aged 65 to 79 and immunocompromised people aged 18 and older, leaving out some people over 50 [3].
  • Crime unit: The new fraud-and-corruption unit will have five Crown attorneys and follows a recommendation from the inquiry into Winnipeg’s police headquarters construction [3].
  • Business measures: Manitoba plans to match the federal capital-investment tax deduction, which Kinew estimated would cost the province nine figures, and freeze Crown land lease increases for a fourth year [3][4].

Perspectives

Manitoba Progressive Conservative Party: Interim leader Konrad Narth called the speech a repeat of the 2023 campaign and said his party’s proposal to exempt the first $30,000 of income from provincial tax would offer more measurable savings [3].

Sources: CBC News

Manitoba Nurses Union: President Darlene Jackson said the speech included no dedicated funding to begin implementing nurse-to-patient ratios, and warned that opening more emergency departments without adding staff could shift nurses between facilities [1].

Sources: The Toronto Star

Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada: President Karen Rees said regulatory certainty and more efficient permitting could help attract investment and advance mineral projects [4].

Sources: The Globe and Mail

item.title: Gravitational-wave data point to black holes born without supernovas
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (Science / Black Holes)
item.description: A team led by California Institute of Technology astrophysicist Katerina Chatziioannou found that black holes about 10 times the Sun’s mass dominate a sample of 257 black-hole mergers, while objects in the 12-to-16-solar-mass range are unusually scarce. The pattern in gravitational-wave observations suggests some massive stars may collapse into black holes without exploding as supernovas [1][2][3]. The researchers also found a narrower range of spins among the roughly 10-solar-mass black holes, supporting the possibility that they share a formation process. Failed supernovas have not been definitively observed, and the team says further analyses and observations are needed to test whether they explain the pattern [1][2][3].
item.content:encoded:
Gravitational-wave data point to black holes born without supernovas

Category: Science

A team led by California Institute of Technology astrophysicist Katerina Chatziioannou found that black holes about 10 times the Sun’s mass dominate a sample of 257 black-hole mergers, while objects in the 12-to-16-solar-mass range are unusually scarce. The pattern in gravitational-wave observations suggests some massive stars may collapse into black holes without exploding as supernovas [1][2][3]. The researchers also found a narrower range of spins among the roughly 10-solar-mass black holes, supporting the possibility that they share a formation process. Failed supernovas have not been definitively observed, and the team says further analyses and observations are needed to test whether they explain the pattern [1][2][3].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

These results represent a connection between the gravitational-wave data and underlying astrophysics we are trying to extract.

— Katerina Chatziioannou, California Institute of Technology astrophysicist (Space.com)

Key Points

  • Hard to observe: A star that collapses without a bright explosion may simply disappear, making failed supernovas difficult to detect directly [1][3].
  • Standard pathway: In the usual account of massive-star death, a supernova ejects the star’s outer material, while its collapsed core can become a neutron star or black hole [2][3].

item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, setting distance record
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (Science / Space Exploration)
item.description: NASA’s Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth on Wednesday, becoming the first human-made object to reach that distance after nearly 50 years in flight [11][17][23]. The probe is now about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) away; a light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours [19]. Voyager 1 remains in interstellar space and continues sending measurements of magnetic fields and plasma waves from its two remaining operational science instruments as its power declines [11][24]. Its measurements provide direct observations of the region beyond the Sun’s protective bubble, including the effects of solar particles reaching into interstellar space [1]. Radio signals now take 24 hours to travel each way: controllers must wait about two days for a command to arrive and a response to return [11][19]. NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory plans a discussion with Voyager team members on Nov. 19 about the probes’ operations, scientific observations and engineering challenges [9].
item.content:encoded:
NASA's Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, setting distance record

Category: Science

NASA’s Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth on Wednesday, becoming the first human-made object to reach that distance after nearly 50 years in flight [11][17][23]. The probe is now about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) away; a light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours [19]. Voyager 1 remains in interstellar space and continues sending measurements of magnetic fields and plasma waves from its two remaining operational science instruments as its power declines [11][24]. Its measurements provide direct observations of the region beyond the Sun’s protective bubble, including the effects of solar particles reaching into interstellar space [1]. Radio signals now take 24 hours to travel each way: controllers must wait about two days for a command to arrive and a response to return [11][19]. NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory plans a discussion with Voyager team members on Nov. 19 about the probes’ operations, scientific observations and engineering challenges [9].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

I feel like this mission is one of the great things that people have ever done, that humans have ever done.

— Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager Interstellar Mission Manager (CBS News)

Did you know: At Voyager 1’s present pace, it would take roughly 18,000 years to travel one light-year from Earth [3].

Key Points

  • Dwindling power: Voyager 1’s generator output has fallen from about 470 watts at launch to a little over 210 watts, and the spacecraft loses roughly 4 watts of available power annually [11][13].
  • Signal strength: Voyager’s 12-foot dish transmits using less power than a typical 40-watt refrigerator bulb, and NASA’s 230-foot Deep Space Network antennas collect the faint signal [11].
  • Twin trajectories: Voyager 1 moves outward at about 3.5 astronomical units a year, compared with Voyager 2’s 3.1, after NASA selected a faster route focused on Jupiter and Saturn [8].
  • Power-saving maneuver: In September, controllers completed a coordinated operation dubbed the “Big Bang,” switching off three devices and substituting lower-power alternatives [17].
  • Public event: The Planetary Society scheduled a Nov. 18 livestream featuring Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd, mission manager Kareem Badaruddin and project scientist Linda Spilker [10].

Perspectives

Alan Cummings, Caltech senior research scientist and former Voyager instrument team member: He described the crossing as an engineering milestone rather than a scientific one, crediting generations of engineers with keeping the spacecraft operational [6].

Sources: Los Angeles Times

Linda Spilker, Voyager project scientist: She said the team did not expect Voyager to keep operating for nearly 50 years; after the 1989 Neptune flyby, she thought the spacecraft might last only a few more years [16].

Sources: Denver7

Deana Weibel, an anthropologist who studies space exploration: She said it was remarkable that Voyager took more than half a typical human lifespan to reach the milestone [1].

Sources: Nature

Timeline

  • 5 September 1977: Voyager 1 launched from Cape Canaveral on its outer-planet mission [19].
  • August 2012: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause and entered interstellar space [19].
  • 20 October 2026: Communications resumed after missed sessions and the activation of backup thrusters [20].
  • 18 November 2026: Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth [11][17].

Technical Details

  • Low-rate uplink: Commands travel to Voyager at 16 bits per second, limiting the amount of command data NASA can send across the one-day signal delay [4].
  • Radioisotope generators: Voyager’s radioisotope thermoelectric generators convert heat from decaying plutonium-238 into electricity [11][13].

Scientific Significance

  • Planetary discoveries: During their outer-planet flybys, the Voyagers found active volcanoes on Jupiter’s moon Io and evidence of a cracked water-ice crust on Europa, which is now thought to hide a potentially habitable ocean [1].
  • Pressure front: An incoming pressure front that began around 2020 caused magnetic fields around the Voyagers to rise sharply before dropping six years later; researchers are investigating the cause [1].

Historical Background

In 1965, doctoral student Gary Flandro identified a rare alignment of the outer planets that would let spacecraft use successive planetary flybys to travel outward [4]. The alignment, which recurs about every 175 years, inspired NASA’s Grand Tour concept, but the four-probe plan was canceled after budget cuts in the early 1970s [4]. NASA then reworked the proposal around the less costly Mariner spacecraft design, producing the Voyager missions [4].

Q&A

Q: Does crossing one light-day mark a new boundary in space?

A: No. It is a distance milestone, not a change in the spacecraft’s surroundings or a new boundary [17].

Q: When will Voyager 2 reach the same distance?

A: NASA expects Voyager 2 to reach one light-day from Earth in November 2035 [19].

item.title: Leonid meteor shower peaks with 10 to 15 meteors an hour
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (Science / Astronomy)
item.description: The annual Leonid meteor shower is peaking overnight Tuesday into Wednesday, Nov. 17-18, with observers under dark skies able to see about 10 to 15 meteors an hour [6][2][1]. The meteors come from debris shed by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the Sun roughly every 33 years; scientists do not expect a meteor storm this year [6][3]. The best viewing window is after midnight and before dawn, when the constellation Leo—the shower’s apparent point of origin—rises higher in the sky. The Moon sets around midnight, reducing moonlight during those hours [6][9]. Viewing conditions will vary by region: far northern Scotland is forecast to have more breaks in the clouds, while clouds could hinder viewing in western Washington [2][9].
item.content:encoded:
Leonid meteor shower peaks with 10 to 15 meteors an hour

Category: Science

The annual Leonid meteor shower is peaking overnight Tuesday into Wednesday, Nov. 17-18, with observers under dark skies able to see about 10 to 15 meteors an hour [6][2][1]. The meteors come from debris shed by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the Sun roughly every 33 years; scientists do not expect a meteor storm this year [6][3]. The best viewing window is after midnight and before dawn, when the constellation Leo—the shower’s apparent point of origin—rises higher in the sky. The Moon sets around midnight, reducing moonlight during those hours [6][9]. Viewing conditions will vary by region: far northern Scotland is forecast to have more breaks in the clouds, while clouds could hinder viewing in western Washington [2][9].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Key Points

  • Meteor speed: Leonid particles enter Earth’s atmosphere at up to 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, making them among the fastest meteors visible [2][4].
  • Historic storms: Observers reported as many as 40 Leonids per second at the 1966 storm’s peak; the 1833 storm has been estimated at up to 150,000 an hour [1][6].
  • Nearby planets: Bright Jupiter and Mars appear near the Leonids’ radiant this year and can help skywatchers locate that region of the sky [6][7].
  • Shower activity: Earth passes through the Leonid meteor stream from Oct. 28 through Dec. 7, so meteors may be visible outside the peak night as well [6].

Historical Background

The comet’s returns in 1899 and 1932 went unobserved, and no major meteor storm followed in those years. Its 1998 return produced Leonid showers from 1999 through 2001 [6].

Action Items

  • Choose a dark viewing spot and watch after midnight: Find an open area away from streetlights and give your eyes 20 to 30 minutes to adapt; no telescope or binoculars are needed [2][4].

item.content:encoded:
Earthshot Prize names five climate innovators in Mumbai, awards £1 million each

Category: Science

Prince William, Prince of Wales, announced five winners of the 2026 Earthshot Prize in Mumbai on Nov. 17, awarding each £1 million ($1.3 million) to expand environmental projects. The recipients were Indian electric-vehicle maker Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, campaign group PFAS-Free France, Niue Ocean Wide Trust, offshore wind company Ørsted and Bhutan, which was recognized for forest conservation [5][6]. They were selected from 15 finalists working on clean transport, pollution, marine protection, renewable energy and conservation [5]. The awards coincided with the United Nations COP31 climate talks, where countries have struggled to agree on fossil fuels and climate finance. A U.N. report released in October said the world was on course to exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius warming threshold [4][9]. William called for urgent action, saying, “They will not judge us by the promises we made, but by the world we leave behind” [4].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

They will not judge us by the promises we made, but by the world we leave behind.

— Prince William, Prince of Wales (Reuters)

Key Points

  • Student projects: A separate children’s challenge reached nearly one million students in 15,000 schools across 24 Indian states; five school teams received awards [8].
  • Air filter: A student-built, electricity-free filter using jute, biochar, bamboo silica, zeolite and cotton lowered reported PM2.5 readings from 98 to 12–30 in tests [8].
  • Forest protection: Bhutan’s conservation efforts were recognized for safeguarding water security for 1.6 billion people in South Asia; the country plans restoration across 50,000 hectares [6].
  • Ocean area: Niue Ocean Wide Trust’s conservation initiative covers more than 327,000 square kilometres of ocean, according to Sky News [10].

Perspectives

Prince William, Prince of Wales: He said he believed people were rising to meet the climate challenge and that positive change could become “irreversible” this decade [4].

Sources: Reuters

Jason Knauf, chief executive of the Earthshot Prize: He said children’s winning projects showed that young people are already taking innovative environmental action rather than waiting for the future [8].

Sources: The Hindu

Princess Catherine, Princess of Wales: She warned that species are being lost as habitats disappear and landscapes change, and said innovators are finding ways to protect and restore the natural world [10].

Sources: Sky News

Timeline

  • December 2019: William introduced the Earthshot idea after two years of development [12].
  • 2020: The Royal Foundation established the environmental prize [5][12].
  • 17 November 2026: Five winners were named at the Mumbai awards ceremony [5][6].
  • 30 November 2026: The awards ceremony is scheduled to stream on Prime Video [12].

Historical Background

Inspired by former U.S. President John F. Kennedy’s Moonshot challenge, the Earthshot Prize aims to help repair the planet by 2030 [12][6].

Q&A

Q: What is the children’s Earthshot challenge?

A: It invited students aged 9 to 17 to identify environmental problems and develop solutions across the prize’s five areas [8].

Q: What support do winners receive beyond the prize money?

A: The prize connects winners with partners, investors and experts who can help expand their projects [5][12].
